requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
The tests adequately check each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`. All five tests are in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` under `mod[tests]`, and each carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

- **Methods, test functions and helpers are included.** `fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` uses a fixture with an impl method, a `#[test]` function and a helper function in a `cfg(test)` module. It asserts `#impl[S]/fn[method]`, `#mod[tests]/fn[case]` and `#mod[tests]/fn[helper]` each appear as "zero execution".
- **Default trait methods are included, and bodiless declarations are not.** `fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` asserts `#trait[T]/fn[body]: zero execution` and that `fn[declaration]` never appears in the report. It also calls `inventory` directly on a trait that has only a declaration. That call reports no obligations.
- **Macro invocations and derives create no obligations.** In the same test, `inventory` is called on a macro invocation and on a derive, and neither creates an obligation. This is not a clause the requirement names.
- **First-party scope follows the parsing requirement.** `fn[post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor]` has the check fail on `src/vendor/first_party.rs`. It asserts that a root `vendor/foreign.rs` is absent. I checked the report format in `fn[check_saved]`. Both file lines and function lines start with `- {file}`, so the absence assertion is not vacuous.
- **Discovery and parse failures fail the check.** `fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` corrupts the git index. It asserts the check fails with "cannot discover reference sources". `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` writes malformed Rust. It asserts the check fails with "cannot parse rust source".
- **Unmeasurable functions are reported as not measured.** `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` and `#fn[missing]: not measured`. It also checks that a file with no obligations is reported as "no executable obligations — pass".
- **Build-configuration exclusions are not silently dropped.** `fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` asserts `#fn[excluded]: not measured` for a `#[cfg(any())]` function, and that the run fails. The exception-evidence part is cited and belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, not to this subject.
- **Nested functions and closures.** `fn[overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent]` shows nested functions and closures are separate obligations. A covered inner function or closure does not cover the outer function.

I found no scenario the requirement names that these tests would let a violating implementation pass.

text: :::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
